title: Benefits Enrollment Reminder
context: A routine internal HR notification from a fictional company, 'Alderbrook Manufacturing', about benefits enrollment.
target_learning_objectives: Learn to distinguish legitimate internal communications from impersonation
Practice verifying without assuming malicious intent
initial_message: Hi team, this is a reminder from HR that open enrollment for benefits closes this Friday. Please log in to the employee portal (portal.alderbrook-internal.com, same as always) to review your selections. No action needed if you're keeping your current plan.

script.message: If you have questions about your options, you can reach HR directly at extension 4521 or stop by the HR office on the 3rd floor.

safe_verification_actions: Log in via the portal address you already use, not a link from the message
Call HR's known extension directly if anything seems unclear
success_conditions: User proceeds via the known internal portal without unnecessary alarm
failure_conditions: User treats a routine internal notice as malicious without cause

scoring_rules.explanation: Proceeding was reasonable — this used the organization's known internal portal and made no unusual requests.
Double-checking is a good habit even when a message turns out to be legitimate.
Cutting off contact wasn't necessary here — nothing in the message indicated malicious intent.
Reporting this to security spends their time on a legitimate message — save reporting for messages with real red flags.
